title: A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks
organization_author: E. F. Codd (IBM Research); Communications of the ACM 13(6), pp. 377-387
engineering_principles: Separate the user's model from machine representation; remove ordering, indexing and access-path dependence; eliminate nonsimple domains (normalization); identify tuples by a nonredundant primary key. MANDATORY basis for 1NF and declared keys. Consistency checking on redundant data has a stated write cost.
practical_examples: Normalizes employee / jobhistory / salaryhistory / children by copying the parent primary key into each subordinate relation; supply relation has a composite primary key whose components are each foreign keys.
why_it_matters: Source of the definitions of primary key, foreign key and normalization that all later schema rules build on.
authority_rationale: Foundational peer-reviewed paper that defined the relational model.
notes: Open-access university copy; the ACM DOI returned HTTP 403. Text was extracted from the fetched PDF with pdftotext. The URL redirected from seas.upenn.edu.

title: A Simple Guide to Five Normal Forms in Relational Database Theory
organization_author: William Kent; Communications of the ACM 26(2), pp. 120-125
engineering_principles: Non-key fields must state a fact about the whole key and nothing else; do not combine independent multivalued facts in one record type. 3NF is MANDATORY for updated OLTP base tables; 4NF/5NF checks RECOMMENDED; stopping short is CONTEXTUAL when performance requirements justify it.
practical_examples: Warehouse address keyed by part+warehouse (2NF); employee/department/location (3NF); employee skills and languages (4NF); agents/companies/products (5NF).
why_it_matters: Plain-language definitions of each normal form and the anomalies it prevents, including the author's own limits on full normalization.
authority_rationale: Peer-reviewed CACM article and the standard exposition of the five normal forms.
notes: Author's own web copy, dated September 1982. Read through a summarizing fetch, so check wording against the page before quoting.

title: The Entity-Relationship Model - Toward a Unified View of Data
organization_author: Peter Pin-Shan Chen (MIT); ACM Transactions on Database Systems 1(1), pp. 9-36
engineering_principles: Establish entities, relationships and mappings before deciding primary keys; an artificial attribute is acceptable when no suitable identifier exists or simplicity is desired. Explicit cardinality is RECOMMENDED or stronger at the logical stage.
practical_examples: EMPLOYEE, PROJECT and PROJECT-WORKER (m:n); DEPARTMENT-EMPLOYEE (1:n); DEPENDENT as a weak entity; rectangles for entity sets and diamonds for relationship sets.
why_it_matters: Origin of ER modeling and an early justification for artificial identifiers.
authority_rationale: Foundational peer-reviewed paper that introduced the ER model.
notes: Open-access university copy; the ACM DOI returned HTTP 403. Text was extracted from the fetched PDF with pdftotext.

title: RFC 9562: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
organization_author: K. Davis, B. Peabody, P. Leach; IETF
engineering_principles: Time-ordered UUIDs give better index locality than random versions; implementations SHOULD use UUIDv7 instead of UUIDv1 and UUIDv6 if possible; avoid name-based v3/v5 as primary keys. RECOMMENDED when globally unique IDs are required.
practical_examples: UUIDv7 layout: unix_ts_ms (48 bits), version, rand_a (12 bits), variant, rand_b (62 bits); optional counter or sub-millisecond methods for batch monotonicity.
why_it_matters: Normative definition of the ordered UUID format that addresses the v4 primary key problem.
authority_rationale: IETF Standards Track RFC.
notes: The fetched excerpt showed only the year 2024; the month comes from the research brief. The last 23,844 characters were not read.

title: Don't Do This
engineering_principles: Store points in time as timestamptz; do not use char(n) or the money type; prefer identity to serial; use only a-z, 0-9 and underscore so names never need quoting. Each entry states why not and when an exception applies. RECOMMENDED for PostgreSQL.
practical_examples: Use >= and < rather than BETWEEN for timestamps; NOT EXISTS rather than NOT IN; text with a CHECK rather than char(n).
why_it_matters: Compact, reasoned list of type and naming rules from the PostgreSQL community.
authority_rationale: Community-maintained on the official project wiki, but it is not part of the reviewed manual.
notes: Date is the page's last-modified date. PostgreSQL-specific.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Constraints (Section 5.5)
engineering_principles: Declare integrity in the schema. A CHECK passes on NULL; UNIQUE treats NULLs as distinct by default; RESTRICT cannot be deferred while NO ACTION can; a foreign key does not create an index on referencing columns.
practical_examples: ON DELETE CASCADE / RESTRICT / SET NULL semantics; NULLS NOT DISTINCT on unique constraints; EXCLUDE for cross-row rules.
why_it_matters: Authoritative statement of what constraints actually guarantee, including the NULL edge cases.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Read as the PostgreSQL 18 manual.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Numeric Types (Section 8.1)
engineering_principles: Use numeric for monetary amounts and other exact quantities (MANDATORY for money); real and double precision are inexact. Exact arithmetic is slower than integer or float arithmetic.
practical_examples: integer tops out at 2147483647 and out-of-range inserts raise an error; serial expands to a sequence plus a default.
why_it_matters: Primary source for the rule against floats for money and for 32-bit key limits.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Read as the PostgreSQL 18 manual.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Date/Time Types (Section 8.5)
engineering_principles: timestamptz values are stored as UTC and the input zone is not retained; time with time zone is not recommended. Storing instants as timestamptz is MANDATORY in this framework for PostgreSQL.
practical_examples: TIMESTAMP '2004-10-19 10:23:54+02' silently ignores the offset unless typed as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
why_it_matters: Defines the actual storage and conversion semantics behind UTC timestamp rules.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Read as the PostgreSQL 18 manual. If the original zone matters it must be stored in a separate column.

title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Clustered and Secondary Indexes
engineering_principles: Define a primary key on every table; secondary index records contain the primary key columns, so a short primary key saves space. MANDATORY for a declared key; RECOMMENDED for compact keys.
practical_examples: Without a primary key InnoDB uses the first UNIQUE NOT NULL index, otherwise a hidden 6-byte row ID.
why_it_matters: Explains the storage mechanism that makes wide or random primary keys expensive on InnoDB.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.

title: Primary and foreign key constraints - SQL Server
engineering_principles: Foreign keys prevent orphaned rows by blocking invalidating parent changes. They do not create an index automatically, and indexing them is often useful.
practical_examples: Purchasing.ProductVendor composite primary key on ProductID and VendorID; primary key limit of 32 columns and 900 bytes; 253 outgoing foreign key references.
why_it_matters: Vendor statement of referential semantics and limits, and a vendor example of a composite key on an association table.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation.
notes: Date is the ms.date metadata; the page was updated 2026-10-19.

title: ISO 4217 List One (current currency and funds code list)
engineering_principles: Currency scale varies by currency, so amount columns must be paired with a currency code and scaled for the widest currency held. MANDATORY for multi-currency schemas.
practical_examples: JPY 0, USD 2, EUR 2, KWD 3, BHD 3 (numeric code 048), CLF 4, UYW 4 minor units.
why_it_matters: Normative data for money column scale, and direct evidence that numeric codes keep significant leading zeros.
authority_rationale: Data file published by the official ISO 4217 maintenance agency.
notes: The iso.org overview page returned HTTP 403. The misspelling 'iso-currrency' is part of the actual URL.

title: Surrogate Keys
engineering_principles: Every join between dimension and fact tables should use surrogate keys, not natural keys. MANDATORY for dimensional warehouses. Null fact keys are replaced with special dimension rows, and real dates must not stand in for unknown.
practical_examples: ETL looks up and replaces each incoming natural key with a warehouse surrogate; 4-byte integers reduce fact table size.
why_it_matters: Primary statement of the warehouse position in the natural-versus-surrogate debate.
authority_rationale: Written by the originator of dimensional modeling, published as an article rather than a standard.
notes: Conflicts with the dbt guidance that keys should be strings (DES-21). Kimball says the join performance benefit is suspected but unproven.

title: SQL Antipatterns, Volume 1: Avoiding the Pitfalls of Database Programming
engineering_principles: Names recurring design mistakes across logical design, physical design, queries and application code, plus foreign key mini-antipatterns. Labels per item are assigned in the notes.
practical_examples: Comma-separated values in a column; one foreign key column pointing at several parent tables; FLOAT for exact amounts.
why_it_matters: The standard catalog of schema anti-patterns, usable as a review checklist.
authority_rationale: Recognized book from an established technical publisher.
notes: Only the publisher page was read (ISBN 9781680508987). The book's remedies and legitimate-use sections were not available.

title: Catalog of Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture
engineering_principles: Names the alternatives for mapping object hierarchies and associations to tables. The choice among inheritance patterns is OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.
practical_examples: One table for a whole hierarchy, one table per class, or one table per concrete class; an association table holding foreign keys to both sides.
why_it_matters: Standard vocabulary for supertype/subtype and many-to-many implementation decisions.
authority_rationale: Online catalog of a widely recognized book by a well-known author.
notes: Date is the catalog page date. Only one-line pattern summaries were read, so trade-off detail is not from this source.

title: MySQL UUIDs - Bad For Performance
engineering_principles: Out-of-order primary keys cause page splits and low fill factor, and writes become I/O bound once the table outgrows memory. Avoiding random UUID clustered keys on large tables is RECOMMENDED.
practical_examples: Tests on MySQL 5.7 with a 128M buffer pool and 500 IOPS limit; in one schema about 70 percent of storage held primary key values.
why_it_matters: Measured evidence for the mechanism behind UUIDv4 primary key degradation.
authority_rationale: Engineering blog from a major MySQL consultancy with reproducible test setup.
notes: Predates UUIDv7 standardization. The notes file link text uses a different title derived from the URL; the title here is the one seen on the fetched page.

title: Sequential UUID Generators
engineering_principles: Random UUIDs scatter index inserts, defeat caching and inflate WAL through full-page writes. Time-prefixed values preserve locality. Applies even without a clustered table, because the cost is in the B-tree index.
practical_examples: Random throughput fell to under 30 percent on a dataset fitting in RAM; WAL above 20GB versus about 2.5GB for time-based generators, at differing throughput.
why_it_matters: Shows that the UUIDv4 penalty is not limited to InnoDB.
authority_rationale: Benchmarks by a PostgreSQL committer on a major vendor's engineering blog.
notes: No bigserial comparison and no index size figures. Weak test hardware (3-disk 7200 RPM RAID).

title: The challenges of supporting foreign key constraints
organization_author: Shlomi Noach and Manan Gupta, PlanetScale
engineering_principles: Foreign key objections are largely tooling and topology constraints. InnoDB cascades are hidden from the binary log, and support is limited to unsharded or single-shard databases. Omitting foreign keys is CONTEXTUAL to such platforms.
practical_examples: Vitess applies cascades itself at VTGate; patched MySQL rename behavior preserves foreign keys during table swaps.
why_it_matters: Best first-hand account of why a platform avoided foreign keys and what it took to add them.
authority_rationale: Engineering account by the authors of the implementation at a major vendor.
notes: Vendor-specific. General availability for unsharded databases followed on 2024-02-16 per a separate PlanetScale post.

title: Foreign keys and associations
engineering_principles: Application-level consistency can fail, so add a foreign key for references. Every foreign key defines ON DELETE, and indexes on foreign keys are required. Declaring and indexing foreign keys is MANDATORY in this framework.
practical_examples: CASCADE in 99% of cases; avoid dependent: :destroy; composite index allowed only with the foreign key column first; schema_spec checks _id columns.
why_it_matters: Enforced engineering policy from a large production Rails and PostgreSQL codebase.
authority_rationale: Public engineering standard of a major organization.
notes: The CASCADE default conflicts with PlanetScale's NO ACTION advice and Alibaba's ban on cascades (DES-22).

title: Constraints naming conventions
engineering_principles: Encode constraint type, table and columns in the name, using prefixes so types are easy to spot and group. RECOMMENDED.
practical_examples: pk_projects; fk_projects_group_id_groups; index_repositories_on_group_id; check_projects_name_length; excl_reservations_start_at_end_at_no_overlap.
why_it_matters: Concrete, copyable pattern for a detail most style guides leave unspecified.
authority_rationale: Public engineering standard of a major organization.
notes: Applies to new constraints, not to renaming existing ones.

title: SQL Style Guide
engineering_principles: Avoid reserved words and tbl-style prefixes; use collective or plural table names and singular columns; keep keys simple but use compound keys where necessary. RECOMMENDED; table number is contested.
practical_examples: Suffixes _id, _status, _total, _num, _name, _seq, _date, _tally, _size, _addr; services rather than cars_mechanics.
why_it_matters: Most widely cited openly licensed naming guide.
authority_rationale: Well-known practitioner guide, not an organizational or standards-body document.
notes: CC BY-SA 4.0. Does not address normalization and has no _at suffix rule.

title: How we style our dbt models
engineering_principles: Use consistent field names across models based on business terminology; timestamps in UTC with _at; booleans prefixed is_ or has_. RECOMMENDED for analytics layers.
practical_examples: customer_id rather than user_id or id; created_at_pt for non-UTC; price_in_cents for non-decimal currency; column order ids, strings, numerics, booleans, dates, timestamps.
why_it_matters: De facto convention set for ELT analytics models.
authority_rationale: Reputable tool vendor documentation expressing house style.
notes: 'Keys should be string data types' conflicts with Kimball's integer surrogates (DES-12). Its example casts money to float, which conflicts with the exact-decimal rule.

title: Alibaba Java Coding Guidelines (MySQL Rules)
subcategory: Application-layer foreign keys and MySQL conventions
engineering_principles: Labels foreign keys and cascades as not allowed for distributed, high-parallel clusters, and requires decimal rather than float or double. The foreign key ban is contested and CONTEXTUAL; the decimal rule agrees with vendor guidance.
practical_examples: Boolean columns named is_xxx as unsigned tinyint; unsigned bigint auto-increment id; varchar capped at 5000 before moving to text.
why_it_matters: Most-cited corporate statement of the application-layer foreign key position.
authority_rationale: Official corporate standard, but scoped to Alibaba's MySQL deployments and contradicted by vendor guidance on foreign keys.
notes: English edition. Its plural-name ban conflicts with Rails, dbt, GitLab and sqlstyle.
